title: fix(examples,docs): retire the phantom `color` key on `ui:text`, and paint the three tiles with `className`
body:
Fixes #7444

`text-with-colors.json` authored `color` on three `text` nodes and
`content/docs/components/basic/text.mdx` taught it in the same fence as the keys
that work. It is authored, accepted, and does nothing.

## Re-measured on `6bca0e4e8`, each reading with its control

| layer | reading | control that proves the instrument fires |
|---|---|---|
| **Not declared** | `color` in the `TextSchema` interface body (`packages/types/src/layout.ts`) = **0**; in the Zod mirror body (`packages/types/src/zod/layout.zod.ts`) = **0** | `variant` in the same two bodies = **2** and **2** |
| **Not read** | `color` in `packages/components/src/renderers/basic/text.tsx` = **0** — it reads `content`, `variant`, `align`, `className` | `schema.className` in that file = **7**; a repo-wide grep for a root-level `color` read returns exactly one hit, `renderers/basic/icon.tsx:119`, whose `IconSchema` **does** declare `color` — so the grep demonstrably fires when a reader exists |
| **Cannot leak** | `SDUI_DOM_PASS_THROUGH_KEYS` (`packages/core/src/utils/dom-props.ts`) is a closed 8-entry list and `color` is not on it | `className` **is** on it |

## Why nothing went red

`BaseSchema` ends `}).passthrough()` (`packages/types/src/zod/base.zod.ts:241`),
and `TextSchema` is `BaseSchema.extend(...)`. **`.passthrough()` lets any
undeclared key through silently, so no instrument ever speaks.** Measured
directly against the fixture, before this PR:

```
safeValidateSchema(text-with-colors.json).success = true
parsed children keys: [["color","content","type"], x3]
`color` SURVIVED the parse on n nodes = 3
CONTROL undeclared `totallyMadeUpKey` accepted = true | survived parse = true
CONTROL off-enum `variant: "muted"` accepted = false
CONTROL retired `value` accepted     = false
```

The two controls are the point: the validator **is** awake — it refuses an
off-enum `variant` and refuses the retired `value` **by name** — so a named
refusal is perfectly expressible here. `color` was accepted for one reason only,
the same reason a key I invented on the spot was accepted: nothing declared it.

The docs half is the other end of the same hole. The line lived in a
` ```plaintext ` fence, and `check:doc-snippets` collects only
`TS_FENCE_LANGUAGES = new Set(['ts', 'tsx', 'typescript'])`
(`scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs:445`), while `check:doc-types` judges
`type` literals. Deleting the line moved neither gate's counters by one:
`check:doc-types` printed `1105 code block(s), 886 type literal(s)` before and
after, `check:doc-snippets` printed `455 of 455 block(s) judged` before and
after. **This card is a known corpus point for objectui#7418 / objectui#7851** —
no gate reads the non-type keys of a fence under `content/docs/`. No gate is
built here; objectui#7851 is that report-only sweep and it is in flight.

## What changed

**The fixture is not deleted and its name still fits.** The three nodes now
author `className`, which the renderer already forwards
(`text.tsx:151`, `cn(variantClass, alignClass, schema.className || ...)`), so the
entry demonstrates the one working colour channel instead of a phantom. That is
Option A exactly as objectui#7444 words it — *"authors colour text with
`className`, which the renderer already forwards"* — and it is Clause-② `no`:
`className` is declared on both faces (`base.ts:102`, `base.zod.ts:112`) and
read. No key added, no Zod change, no renderer change, no gate change.

Rendered through the real `SchemaRenderer` (`react-dom/server`):

- **before** — `div.flex` with three **bare text children**: no element, no
  class, no colour, and `color=` never appears as an attribute. The published
  "Colored Text" section showed three identically-unstyled strings.
- **after** — `div.flex` containing `span.text-primary`,
  `span.text-destructive` and `span.text-muted-foreground`.

It renders differently, which is the objectui#6318 standard the corpus test
records: a "correction" that changes no pixel is evidence the schema was at
fault instead.

## The surface widened by one file, and why

That render change moved a pin: `layout-dom-leak-5574.test.tsx`'s `NODE_CENSUS`
went `text.noElement` **162 -> 159**, because those three nodes left the
fragment arm for the `span` arm. This is not a new decision — the pin's own
comment already records objectui#6942 doing the identical thing (`176 -> 162`,
*"the census moving in the SAFE direction: fewer phantom-clean nodes, more
elements actually read"*), and its assertion message asks for the number to be
updated when the catalog is re-authored. The commit updates that one number, the
two prose restatements of it, and records the reason.

⚠️ This is one file beyond the two the card scoped, so it is declared rather
than quiet. Checked before touching it: no open PR in the repo touches
`layout-dom-leak-5574.test.tsx` (all 22 open PRs enumerated; objectui#7860's
claim on `examples/schema-catalog/test/` is `safe-validate-corpus-6318.test.ts`
only), and nothing else in the diff enters that directory.

## Evidence

Gate union re-run on the pushed commit **`f7ae4581c`**, with
`git diff HEAD` empty:

```
check:doc-types      ✅  Every documented component type is registered.
check:doc-snippets   Every covered documentation snippet compiles against the built types.
check:doc-fences     ✅  every TypeScript block in 227 document(s) is fenced ts/tsx/typescript …
check:control-bytes  ✅  check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 6369 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary).
check:docs-route-closure / check:doc-example-readers / check:shell-escape-residue /
check:vi-mock-specifiers / check:vi-mock-inherit — all EXIT=0
vitest examples/schema-catalog/   Test Files 28 passed (28) · Tests 2075 passed (2075)
tsc -p tsconfig.test.json         EXIT=0, and --listFiles confirms the edited test file is in its input set
regenerate:check                  examples/schema-catalog/src/index.ts is up to date (431 entries)
```

⛔ "Still green" is not the evidence here — all of these were green **while the
defect was present** (28/28 files, 2075/2075 tests, both doc gates, on the
unmodified tree). The evidence that the defect existed is the controlled
readings above; the evidence it is gone is the render diff.

The one instrument that did speak spoke **only after the fix**: the census pin
went red at `159` vs `162` on the first post-fix run. That is a corpus census,
not a contract check — it noticed three nodes starting to render, and would have
stayed silent forever had they kept authoring a key nothing reads.

Changeset, verdict quoted verbatim:

```
Compared the working tree with 6bca0e4e8 (merge-base with origin/main): 3 file(s)
changed, 0 of them published source of a package the release covers, 0 of them a
manifest whose published contract moved, 0 under a package changesets ignores, 0
changeset(s) added.
✅  No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range,
so no changeset is owed.
```

Acted on: no changeset added.

**Not run, plainly:** the full repo `pnpm lint` and the full test suite. Lint was
narrowed to the three changed files and the narrowing is measured, not assumed —
`--format json` judged 3/3, and eslint's own config reports `.mdx` and `.json` as
*"File ignored because no matching configuration was supplied"*, so the only
eslint-governed file in this diff is the `.tsx`, which is clean (0 errors, 0
warnings); `eslint.config.js` declares no `parserOptions.project` or
`projectService`, so linting is not type-aware and this diff cannot move the
verdict of any file it does not touch. CI runs the farm regardless.
